insight.title: Why Free Shipping Makes You Spend More
insight.subtitle: The strange math of buying things you don't want just to avoid a delivery fee.
insight.notificationHook: Free shipping usually costs you more

sections.text: To avoid a $5 shipping fee, we routinely add a $15 item we don’t need to our online shopping cart. We call this saving money, but our bank account disagrees.

Retailers strategically set free-shipping thresholds just above their average order value. This forces you to make a choice: pay for an invisible service (shipping) or buy a tangible asset (a product).
Because humans hate paying for "ghost" services like delivery, we gladly overspend on clutter. The retailer clears inventory, while we end up with drawers full of unwanted socks and lip balms.
We willingly spend fifteen dollars to save five.
